correctness.rationale: The 1-indexed sequence, chronological permutation and left multiplication fix the sign of the result. Each A_i squares to zero and entry (1,3) is supplied only by A_1 A_2. In separate time steps this contributes once per ordered-in-time pair; within a step it contributes exactly when operator 2 occurs before 1. Thus the exact difference from T^2/2 is h^2 D(N)/2. The six decoder bins have signs -,-,+,+,-,+. On the consecutive intervals cut by 1/3,2/3,5/6, the four-point sum at (x+j)/4 for j=0..3 takes values -2,2,0,0, agreeing with f+g; the two half-scale g terms cancel exactly. Summing complete four-point blocks and removing the zero-index term leaves the odd-prefix increment. With m=2r+1 and x=phi_2(r), the remaining evaluations have cuts at 1/3 and 2/3, and on each of the three pieces the sum is -2. Dyadic inputs cannot hit those non-dyadic cuts. So D(4m+1)=D(m)-2, D(3)=-1, and N_1=3, N_(k+1)=4N_k+1, proving the exact formula on all k. Since log N_k=k log 4+O(1), the normalized entry has the claimed limit, and any fixed subordinate norm bounds its magnitude up to a constant. The proof is a subsequence lower bound for the specified decoder, not a lower bound at every N.
